chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqoub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, who said:

A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while we were in his presence: 'May I be sacrificed for you, we fear that due to our sins we will be lodged in the dwellings of the weak ones (of understanding).' He said: 'No, by Allah, Allah will not do that with you ever.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a common honorific phrase)
key_terms.لَا وَ اللَّهِ: No, by Allah (an emphatic negative response)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about the fear of being among the weak ones due to sins?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) comforts a companion who fears that his sins might relegate him to the status of *al-mustad'ifin* (the weak or deficient in understanding/faith). The Imam’s emphatic assurance—'By Allah, Allah will never do that to you'—highlights the Shia theological principle of divine mercy (*rahmah*) and the concept of *al-aman* (security) for the faithful, suggesting that while sins may cause temporary deficiency, they do not necessarily result in permanent exclusion from God's grace for those who remain attached to the Ahl al-Bayt.
